title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference | Week 4 vs. New York Giants
headline: LaFleur calls Trey McBride 'elite of the elite' and says the offense is still working on explosive plays and pre-snap penalties. Giants edge Brian Burns is out for Week 4.
summary: LaFleur spent much of the session on the league-wide shift toward tight ends. He said defenses are staying in shells and limiting explosives, which pushes offenses toward the run game and short passes with yards after the catch. He was highly complimentary of Trey McBride as a pass catcher and a run blocker, and he said he is glad to have the tight end he mentioned as 'Tip' after wishing the Cardinals hadn't drafted him. He said Arizona has faced three heavy-zone teams (Chargers, Seattle, San Francisco), which explains some of the missing explosives. He still wants better play-calling, clarity and detail, and said the pre-snap penalties are on the coaches to fix, including mixing up the snap cadence. He said his offense will evolve over the season, and he cited last year's late-season use of 13 personnel in LA. Max Melton and Denzel Burke 'responded well' to bigger roles last week, and LaFleur said he has a lot of confidence in both. He told Walter Nolen to keep going despite the lack of pass-rush production. On the Giants, he called their front seven loaded, noted Brian Burns is out, praised Abdul Carter, and said Jameis Winston can throw for 500 yards at any moment.

signals.note: Burke also got a bigger role last week and keeps the coach's confidence, so he is likely to stay on the field in the secondary.
signals.quote: I got a lot of confidence in DB as well.

signals.note: Nolen is playing inside without much pass-rush production yet. LaFleur backed his effort but gave no specifics, so he is a wait-and-see IDP.

topics.detail: LaFleur said defenses are limiting explosives and sitting in shells, and teams are reluctant to match bigger tight ends. That leads offenses to run more and rely on YAC passing. He said he builds from a foundation of what his players do well and avoids over-complicating the offense.

Arizona has faced three zone-heavy defenses, and LaFleur said early-season numbers are a mirage. He also said the offense needs to call the right play at the right time and connect on the second and third levels.
LaFleur called the pre-snap penalties the real problem and put it on the coaches. He said they will keep varying the snap cadence and will not settle for being average.

He said his offenses always look different in Week 17 than in Week 3, citing 2016 Atlanta and last year's LA team's use of 13 personnel. He does not know what Arizona will look like later in the year.

Brian Burns is out, but LaFleur called the front seven loaded and said Abdul Carter keeps getting better. He said Jameis Winston is high-risk, high-reward and can put up big yardage at any time. He also called a big opposing player a 'load' who is hard to tackle, though the player was unclear from the captions.

LaFleur blamed the lack of pressure partly on game script and Seattle's max protection. He said San Francisco's offense, which has yet to give up a sack to Arizona, deserves credit. His message to the defense was to keep working.
LaFleur would rather not bring back defensive pass interference challenges, calling the calls subjective.

headline: Lamar Jackson was limited in practice with something minor (Minter sounded unconcerned), while two injured centers are out long term and the offensive line is being reshuffled.
summary: Minter opened by calming fears over Lamar Jackson, saying he practiced in a limited role with a small issue after early worry that he wasn't on the field. The team's focus is on its own execution rather than the opponent, though he praised Titans rookie QB Cam Ward as talented and now helped by a stable offensive coordinator, Brian Daboll. He called Tennessee's interior D-line one of the best and said they have two good backs and outside weapons, including Carnell Tate. Two injured centers (the description names Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic) are not 100% confirmed as season-ending but are definitely long term. For this week Baltimore will lean on in-house options at center while adding new pieces such as Andre James for depth and the longer view. A rookie who can play three positions along the line was praised for his flexibility, though he was not named. At guard, Andrew Vorhees and Emery Jones will compete, with Minter showing confidence in both. On defense he called for better tackling, more violence at the point of attack, and schematic answers, and he praised Nate Wiggins for bouncing back after a pass interference call.

title: Joe Brady On Team Intensity, Facing The Patriots, And More
headline: Brady says he's not concerned about Josh Allen's health, praises James Cook's bounce-back workhorse game, and keeps Christian Benford's toe injury week-to-week with a chance he plays Sunday vs. the Patriots.
summary: Brady dismissed concern about Josh Allen, saying he isn't worried, though he acknowledged Allen is banged up like everyone after games and that he has to protect him better in both the run and pass game and factor that into play calling. He called the Patriots a tough, well-coached defense that mixes blitz, man and zone, and said the Bills must simply execute against any look and protect the football. He brushed off division-standings talk, stressing a 'nameless, faceless opponent' approach and 'competitive stamina,' which he credited Allen with embodying after a turnover-filled win. On James Cook, he said he trusted him as a bigger-role back since becoming offensive coordinator and praised how Cook rebounded from a bad first play (a fumble, implied) to run well the rest of the game. On Christian Benford's toe, he said the team will take it day by day through the week, noting some players who miss practice still may play Sunday. Defensive lineman Phidarian Mathis is back in the building after a setback and the team is eager to see him practice, though no timeline was given. He said the run defense is improving from game one to three against varied run schemes and that stopping the Patriots' run game, with two good backs, is key. He also defended Drake Maye through his slow start, calling him an outstanding quarterback who will be fine.

Rookie tackle Monroe Freeling is in concussion protocol after symptoms surfaced later on game day. He moved around Wednesday but wasn't cleared, and Canales hopes he practices Thursday. Jaycee Horn and Michael Jackson are both on IR, neither is out for the season, and the rough timeline is about eight weeks, give or take. Xavier Legette is more week-to-week, and Jalen Coker is day-to-day with Thursday a big test. Damien Lewis (elbow) needs about a week, so Corey Bullock is expected to start at guard. title: Ben Johnson on Aaron Glenn, preparing for Jets | Press Conference
headline: Bears QB for Sunday vs. Jets is unannounced: Caleb Williams is improving but out of walkthrough, Case Keenum played well Monday, and Braxton Jones is week to week.
summary: Johnson said it is a big week of decisions about who will be active, with several players' health to be tracked through practice. He praised the Jets as a strong team with top special teams, a high-level offense and a veteran defense, and said Aaron Glenn's play-calling brings unscouted looks. Three quarterbacks are in the mix for Sunday's start, and Johnson said he will pick whoever gives the team the best chance to win. He called Case Keenum's Monday performance decisive and well prepared, said it will factor into the evaluation, and said he feels good about all three QBs. Caleb Williams is getting better daily but will not take part in walkthrough today. Braxton Jones is week to week and not expected to practice, so the Bears are looking at swing tackle options, including Ozzy Trapilo, Jordan McFadden and Joe Thuney. Johnson said the pass catchers want more targets and that getting the ball distributed is on him as play caller. He also praised Malik Muhammad's upward trajectory and said Tyrique Stevenson was limited but returned quickly from injury.

title: HC Sean Payton on continuing to find ways to improve: ‘We’re early in this race'
headline: Payton says Dobbins is 'ready' and the Broncos' first-half run game has been inconsistent; Tillman's health went unanswered ahead of the 49ers game.
summary: Payton spent the session on the Broncos' slow starts. At 2-1, they are near the bottom of the league in first-half scoring and point differential. He said the team recognizes it is not good and has to be fixed in the opening periods of practice and in the early game script. He named the run game as a specific problem: they have not run the ball consistently well in the first half of any of the three games, which he tied to quarterback comfort and time of possession. He was upbeat on J.K. Dobbins, saying he is ready and was re-signed because of his skill set and competitiveness. When asked about Dondrea Tillman and outside linebacker depth, he only said he feels good about the linebacker depth. A player who was seen in a boot practiced fully Wednesday, though the transcript does not make clear who that was. He praised Brock Purdy and the 49ers' offense, which has allowed no sacks in three weeks and is first on third down and in the red zone. He also gave credit to Kyle Shanahan's creativity and recalled evaluating Christian McCaffrey out of college. He said the 17% increase in blitzes against Denver is mostly about opponent schemes and will be clearer in about five weeks. He liked last week's two takeaways but said they are still looking for forced fumbles and want fewer offensive turnovers.

title: Campbell on Goff & Gill-Howard
headline: Goff is durable and the offense stays on its current course. Rookie DL Skyler Gill-Howard got offensive snaps, and the offensive line is improving with Blake Miller and Juice Scruggs settled in.
summary: Campbell previewed Sunday night's road game in Charlotte against a Carolina team coming off a loss. He praised their aggressive defensive front and called Bryce Young's quick release and the big receivers and tight ends problematic. He said the offensive line played much better against the Jets and Buffalo, with Blake Miller back and Christian Mahogany playing well. He said Juice Scruggs is settling in at center, and that continuity among Tate Ratledge, Miller and the others will drive growth. He defended Jared Goff's lack of mobility, calling his game cerebral and saying the offense runs the way it does because of him. He also praised Goff's toughness, saying he plays through unreported ailments and never misses practice. Rookie DL Skyler Gill-Howard earned his offensive snap through urgency and violent execution. Campbell said the 2024 class, including Ennis Rakestraw and Mahogany, is needed for consistency and could take some load off Jahmyr Gibbs. He also explained why Miller was preferred over Monroe in the draft: more starting experience at tackle.

title: Matt LaFleur's message going into Week 4: 'All areas need to improve'
headline: Jayden Reed is done for the season (neck surgery), so WR work will be by committee (Skyy Moore, Bo Melton, J. Michael Sturdivant), while the offense is struggling and the O-line is being rebuilt around new veteran guards.

Michael Sturdivant sharing the load, and Moore's return-game role will not change. After a poor start, LaFleur said the offense needs to improve in every area, including a run game that has not been effective and pass protection that has limited explosive plays. title: DeMeco Ryans on Nico Collins’ Return & Texans vs Cowboys
headline: Nico Collins is back at practice and the Texans will see how his week goes, with no confirmation he'll play Sunday vs. Dallas. Ed Ingram is returning to the line, Azeez Al-Shaair is week to week with a groin injury, and Mario Edwards is out for the season.
summary: Ryans said the team is excited to have Nico Collins back practicing and called him an explosive playmaker who is a threat whenever he is on the field. Asked directly whether Collins will play Sunday, he only said Collins is back practicing today and that they will see how the week goes. On the offense, Ryans said the run game is being reset after inefficiency in the first three games, citing blocking, running and coordination, and that Ed Ingram's return should help with his physical, low-pad style. He said the line will keep its current arrangement for now, so Wyatt Teller's spot is unchanged. Ryans also said motion at the snap has helped the offense, and that he wants efficiency rather than one specific way of moving the ball. Defensively, Mario Edwards is out for the rest of the season, and Azeez Al-Shaair has a groin injury and is week to week. Young linebackers will need to step up, and Kenneth Murray is getting up to speed on the verbiage. Ryans put the defense's middle-of-the-field problems down to missed tackles, and said Reed Blankenship has improved from Week 1 to Week 3. The opponent is Dallas, and Ryans praised CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens as big-time playmakers.

title: Shane Steichen: Midweek update, Colts vs. Commanders
headline: Alec Pierce is out for the time being and the Colts must manufacture chunk plays without him; Daniel Jones is praised (~70% completions), and Ashton Dulin is progressing toward a possible London trip.
summary: Steichen previewed the trip to London to face Washington, which is coming off a big win over Seattle. He expects to prepare for both Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota, since both are mobile and Washington's defense is multiple, with lots of pressures and blitzes. He singled out Stefon Diggs and Terry McLaurin as explosive receivers the Colts must limit. On offense, he admitted that losing Alec Pierce for the time being hurts, because Pierce is a big-play threat. The coaches will have to scheme chunk plays, such as in-breaking or out-breaking routes that go for big yardage. He defended Daniel Jones's play coming off the Achilles surgery, saying Jones is completing close to 70% and that the real issue is holding on to the ball in the pocket. Darius Slayton needs more acclimation to the offense before he is active, and the kickoff duties for the kicker are still undecided. He also explained his late-game clock management and field goal philosophy, citing the last-minute slant to Keenan that set up a game-winning kick.

title: Liam Coen on Team Mentality Entering Week 4, Continuing to Respond | Press Conference
headline: Parker Washington's contested-catch ability has earned Trevor Lawrence's trust in key situations, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. is gaining confidence as a downhill runner after a TD game, while the Jags keep emphasizing the run game ahead of Cincinnati.

He spent a long stretch praising Parker Washington's catch radius, strength at the catch point and run-after-catch ability, comparing his build to Ja'Marr Chase's and saying Trevor Lawrence trusts him in critical situations like third-and-long. Most of the rest of the session was Bengals prep: respect for Dexter Lawrence's disruption, the challenge of Ja'Marr Chase, and Joe Burrow's accuracy and ability to extend plays. The message to the team was a 'goldfish mentality' and a focus on their own response rather than on Cincinnati. Coen said he revisited last year's Denver game only briefly and noted an injury to Denver's nickel. On Chris Rodriguez Jr., he said Rodriguez was frustrated early, that the staff didn't create enough room for him in Weeks 1-2, and that better blocking and momentum last week got him downhill and into the end zone. title: Kevin O'Connell Talks Dolphins Game, Adapting Offense After Injuries, Run Game & Demond Claiborne
headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle sprain) is day-to-day and sat out first practice, with O'Connell noncommittal on Sunday; Aaron Jones is carrying the RB load, Demond Claiborne should get more work, and Gavin Bartholomew's snaps rise with Josh Oliver out.
summary: O'Connell opened by praising Myles Price for his NFC Special Teams Player of the Week honor and previewed a home game against a well-coached Dolphins team. Justin Jefferson, Chuck Demmings and Brett Thorson did not practice; Jefferson is considered day-to-day with an ankle sprain the staff is encouraged about, but O'Connell wouldn't say what it means for the weekend and stressed the team will be smart with him. He took blame for not adjusting well enough to playing most of last week's game without Jefferson, though he praised Jordan Addison's impact, and noted Jauan Jennings is still adjusting to playing multiple positions. On the run game, the Vikings are running a lot, seeing more eight-man fronts, and want to keep committing to it; Jordan Mason is expected back at some point, Aaron Jones has shouldered the load, and Demond Claiborne should get more work out of the backfield. He discussed ways to help Kyler Murray, such as understanding his preference for under-center play action and adjusting timing and protection, and called last week's issues execution one-offs across the whole offense. He also praised the front office for practice squad additions and gave a measured take on reviewing pass interference. Finally, he said he's confident in Gavin Bartholomew, who will see a bigger snap count with Josh Oliver out, though no one replaces Oliver's blocking exactly and T.J. Hockenson leads the group.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 9/30: "We have to be at our best when it's required"
headline: Vrabel publicly backs Drake Maye amid a rumored rift, and the Patriots are shuffling their offensive line ahead of a divisional road game at Buffalo; no skill-position news was given.
summary: Vrabel opened by saying adversity is unavoidable and that the team has to reset quickly after a loss and focus on who is available. He said the roster spots opened by recent injured reserve moves have not been filled, and that one player was just added to the practice squad. Harold Landry is still not ready to start his practice window, though Vrabel said he is working hard to return. He firmly rejected an unnamed-source report of friction with Drake Maye, saying he chose to coach in New England because Maye is the quarterback. He described his coaching of Maye as focused on urgency, huddle command and getting teammates to believe in the play call, not on X's and O's. Asked what he wants schematically, he said more points and fewer negative plays, and criticized the lack of consistent execution and of moving the line of scrimmage. He said the pass catchers can improve like everyone else by winning one-on-one matchups, being where they should be and blocking when they don't have the ball. On the offensive line, Walter Rouse and Ben Brown are working with the first group today and tomorrow, while a bigger move involving Alijah Vera-Tucker is unlikely for now. He also praised Buffalo's offense (Josh Allen, James Cook, Dalton Kincaid) and said the defensive interior needs to produce more pressure and run stuffs.

headline: Odell Beckham Jr. has been released after never getting a real role, and J.J. McCarthy has been added as a quarterback. headline: Sirianni stays committed to the run game and tush push, says rookie WR Makai Lemon's touches will grow as trust builds, and gives no clear answer on the backup QB order.

He declined to say whether Tanner McKee might be the number two QB, saying only that he has faith in everyone in the room. He called the Rams a talented, motivated and well-coached opponent and said the team needs its best game to date.

title: Todd Bowles on Jalon Daniels: Up to the Challenge | Press Conference
headline: Jalon Daniels makes his first NFL start Thursday at Green Bay; Bowles says Trotter did everything in practice, Rueben Bain is uncertain, and Sean Tucker and David Walker are in line for bigger roles.
summary: Bowles said Jalon Daniels, who beat out Browning for the backup job, will make his first NFL start at Green Bay on a short week. He called Daniels a calm, intelligent pocket passer, with the ability to move around only a bonus. The offense will be tailored somewhat to what Daniels is comfortable with, since Baker Mayfield can handle more checks and audibles. Bowles said the protection problems in the last game were shared by the line, the backs and the communication, and that the team has changed some things in practice. Rueben Bain is still being evaluated for a groin, a shoulder and a calf, and the decision will come at the end of the week. Josiah Trotter did everything in practice, with shoulder pads going on Thursday for a better read. Sean Tucker needs to run the ball more, David Walker will definitely get more snaps with Bain out, and Antoine Winfield Jr. needs to be used in more ways to make splash plays. title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Titans OL Fernando Carmona needs surgery and the replacement is a secret (Pat Coogan is a possible option), while Cam Ward's pocket footwork is improving and Saleh isn't worried about Franklin-Myers' back for Sunday.
summary: Saleh opened with the injury report. John Franklin-Myers has a back issue and sat out Wednesday's practice, and two others, 'Tony' and 'Taj', also sat out. Saleh said he isn't overly concerned about any of them for Sunday. Fernando Carmona needs surgery, and Saleh hopes to get him back later in the season. He wouldn't say who replaces him, calling it an open book with every option on the table, and he dodged whether Pat Coogan would play guard or center. Most of the rest of the session was about Cam Ward. Saleh said Ward's footwork and trust in the offensive line are lasting longer into games, though he still reverts to old habits late. He wanted Ward to use his legs more to extend a play against the Giants. Saleh explained the lack of deep shots (six attempts of 20+ yards, none completed, per a reporter) by pointing to two-shell coverages and bad weather. He said the run game has to work to pull safeties down, and it did in the second half last week. He credited slow starts to a fumbled opening kickoff, dropped passes and missed communication, and called the group young but improving. He praised JC Latham as playing at a Pro Bowl level and said the new interior starter is communicating well. Lamar Jackson's running is the main challenge this week.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/30/26
headline: Jayden Daniels is back at practice in a limited jog-through with no Sunday decision until Friday, so Marcus Mariota remains the likely starter. Rachaad White is not practicing with a shoulder issue, and Austin Ekeler is back but not guaranteed to play.
summary: Dan Quinn opened the London week by stressing that routines stay the same despite the travel and the venue. He said everyone on the roster is either full or limited today except Rachaad White, whose shoulder is still sore and needs more treatment. Jayden Daniels will do a jog-through today, which would have been limited work in a full practice. He will add reps through the week, and Quinn expects a definite determination by Friday. He called it too early to call and did not confirm Marcus Mariota as the starter. Daniels will wear an elbow brace all season. Austin Ekeler is back from injury, but Quinn is in no rush: he wants to see how Ekeler handles the workload and the new system and will reassess in about three days. Samuel Cosmi and Nick Cross stayed home to rehab, aiming for next week. Lucas Patrick, who is limited, impressed Quinn at center, and the line combinations are still being sorted out. At linebacker, Frankie Luvu is working back, Kain Medrano is in the mix and Sonny Styles is part of the group. In the secondary, Mike Sainristil moves to nickel and Fabian Moreau gets more reps. Quinn praised the run defense up front and expects Indianapolis to test it with Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones.
